title: Understanding the Filter Condition
text: To filter the DataFrame, you need to select rows where the item is 'banana' and the inventory is at least $$150$$. How can you express this condition using logical operators?

title: Logical Operators in Pandas
text: Remember that in Pandas, you can use '&' for logical AND and '|' for logical OR. How would you use these to filter for bananas with inventory greater than or equal to 150?

title: Constructing the Filter Condition
text: The condition is `(fruit["item"] $$==$$ "banana") & (fruit["inventory"] $$ \geq $$ 150)` — two comparisons joined with `&`, each wrapped in its own parentheses.

title: Sorting the DataFrame
text: After filtering, you need to sort the DataFrame by price in descending order. Which Pandas function allows you to sort a DataFrame?

title: Using sort\_values
text: The function `sort\_values` can be used to sort a DataFrame. What parameters would you use to sort by price in descending order?

title: Sorting by Price
text: Putting it together: `fruit[(fruit["item"] $$==$$ "banana") & (fruit["inventory"] $$ \geq $$ 150)].sort\_values("price", $$ascending=False)`$$ — the filter goes inside `fruit[...]`, and $$`ascending=False`$$ puts the highest price first.
